How article accuracy is tracked on EDFM.

== Verification statuses ==
Recorded via {{tl|Article status}}, always as visible text (never colour alone):

* '''Verified''' — checked directly against current Live gameplay by a named reviewer.
* '''Partially verified''' — some claims checked, others not; the article should say which.
* '''Needs review''' — drafted but not yet checked. Tracked in [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Pages Needing Review]].
* '''Draft''' — incomplete, use {{tl|Draft warning}}.
* '''Historical''' — describes a past state of the game; use {{tl|Historical warning}}.
* '''Legacy only''' — applies to ''Elite Dangerous: Legacy'', not current Live; use {{tl|Legacy warning}}.
* '''Upcoming''' — describes an announced-but-not-yet-released feature; must not be presented as current fact.

== Game modes ==
* '''Live''' — the actively developed, current game.
* '''Legacy''' — the frozen pre-Odyssey-update client, still operated separately.
* '''Both''' — confirmed true in both.
* '''Historical''' — no longer applicable to either; kept for record only.

=== Status "Legacy only" vs. mode "Legacy" ===
These are two different axes and are not redundant with each other:
* '''Mode "Legacy"''' is the routine, per-fact tag — use it any time part of an article's subject differs between Live and Legacy, at any verification status. Pair it with the optional <code>|legacy_differences=</code> field on {{tl|Article status}} to say what actually differs.
* '''Status "Legacy only"''' is reserved for articles that are entirely about a Legacy-exclusive mechanic with no Live counterpart at all — the same relationship "Historical" already has as a status vs. as something you'd note in passing on a Live article.
An article can be Live-mode with a noted Legacy difference; it should not usually be both "Legacy only" status and "Both" mode, since that would mean claiming universal applicability for something defined as Legacy-exclusive.

== What a review means ==
A reviewer records: verification status, game mode, game version/update, last-reviewed date, reviewer identity, an assessment of source quality, and any known uncertainty. These seven fields are always part of {{tl|Article status}}. Two more are optional and used only when relevant: <code>|legacy_differences=</code> (what specifically differs from Live, when mode isn't simply "Both") and <code>|recent_changes=</code> (a one-line pointer to a recent, significant change — for anything longer, use {{tl|Patch history}} instead).

== Uncertain content ==
Use {{tl|Unverified claim}}, {{tl|Estimated information}}, or {{tl|Community observation}} inline rather than stating something as settled fact. A page can be genuinely useful while honestly marking its own gaps.
